card.name: Chennu Nalike
card.tagline: Tulu Mera-community post-harvest ritual dance of Suggi
card.profile: Chennu Nalike is an ancient traditional folk-ritual art practised by the Mera (Moger/Mogera) community of Tulu Nadu, an indigenous, matrilineally organised people of Kasaragod (Kerala) and the Mangalore, Udupi and Coorg districts of Karnataka (Wikipedia). Performed at night after the harvest in the Tulu month of Suggi (around February-March), it begins on Suggi Punnam (full moon) and lasts three to nine days as decided by the community head (Wikipedia). It features two characters, Chennu and Koraga; the Chennu wears a woman's costume with a Sampige flower on the head, while men and women provide background music and sing Paddanas (Tuluva oral epics) (Wikipedia).
card.insight: The Mera belong to the body of Tuluva ritual specialists (alongside Nalike, Parava and Pambada communities) who serve as mediums in Bhuta Kola spirit worship, situating Chennu Nalike within the wider Dravidian ritual cosmology of Tulu Nadu (Wikipedia, Buta Kola).
